nodes.text:
The rumor mill’s favorite recipe

Where did all the “emergency” chatter come from? A quick trace leads us to - you guessed it - good ol’ Falun Gong-affiliated sources. (https://t.co/zU7f2RMsK7)

The same folks who claimed there was a coup in #China some years ago (spoiler: there wasn’t). From there, the story spread faster than actual #HMPV with some media outlets throwing in their own spicy misquotes of Reuters and others
(A scaremongering example from the Indian media 👇)

nodes.author: shamimzakaria
nodes.text: Here’s the kicker: reports of “overflowing hospitals” were, well, not reports at all. I checked. Three hospitals near my home and workplace - no unusual queues, no frenzied staff. Just your average winter crowd battling colds and coughs. And yet, certain news outlets didn’t let facts get in the way of a good old-fashioned “#China’s collapsing” narrative.

nodes.author: shamimzakaria
nodes.text:
Fear sells, facts bore

Let’s be honest. The media isn’t exactly winning Pulitzers for nuance these days. It’s easier (and more profitable) to slap “OUTBREAK” on a headline than to say, “Winter flu season hits, as expected.” Context? Boring. Data? Too complicated. A baseless claim about #China on the verge of a pandemic? Jackpot.

nodes.author: shamimzakaria
nodes.text:
So, should you worry about #HMPV?

Not unless you also plan on panicking every time someone sneezes near you. HMPV is a run-of-the-mill respiratory virus that peaks in winter and spring. Preventing it is no rocket science: wash your hands, avoid crowds if you can, and -

nodes.author: shamimzakaria
nodes.text:
The bigger picture

This “#HMPVOutbreak” isn’t a story about a virus; it’s a story about how narratives are spun. The anti-China echo chamber is alive and well, feeding off anything that can be twisted into a crisis. But here’s the reality: I’m in #China’s capital #Beijing, living my life, and it’s business as usual

nodes.author: shamimzakaria
nodes.text: So, to the media outlets that turned a routine health update into the next global catastrophe: congratulations on the clicks. But next time, maybe try a little less drama and a little more truth. Stay calm, stay informed, and for goodness’ sake, stop believing every sensational headline you see
